newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Corporate tax seen lifting UK Jan PSBR.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Corporate tax seen lifting UK Jan PSBR.

text.p: Substantial corporate tax receipts gathered in January should mean Britain's public finances showed a surplus in the month, but tax changes for thousands of self- employed workers mean the take may be lower than last year.
The consensus forecast in a Reuters poll suggested the data, due at 0930 GMT on Tuesday, will show a surplus of 3.5 billion sterling in January, versus a 2.1 billion deficit in December.
This would bring the cumulative public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) for the year to date to 19.636 billion stg.
"January is a key tax gathering month for the public finances, particularly for corporation tax payments," said David Philpotts at Schroder Economics in London.

But since corporate payments relate to the 1995/6 financial year -- when activity was relatively subdued -- Philpotts said he did not expect the surplus to be as great as in January 1996, when the repayment was 3.7 billion sterling.
A recent move to allow the self employed to assess their own tax position may also have had an adverse affect on the normally high January income, economists said.
The change means a shift in the payment date from January 1 to January 31, which could hit income tax receipts for last month, moving them into February's accounts.
"We have cut one billion stg off our projection for income tax receipts to allow for that factor," said Michael Saunders at Salomon Brothers, who is forecasting a 3.8 billion repayment.

Philpotts, too, said the move to self assessment would take the shine of income tax receipts. He said this, coupled with an absence of privatisation proceeds in January, would reduce the overall size of the surplus.
Philpotts is forecasting a repayment of 2.0 billion sterling.
But Ciaran Barr, economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, was more upbeat, expecting a hefty debt repayment of 4.0 billion sterling, boosted by the corporate taxes.
"We also look for further restraint in government spending," he said.
For the year as a whole, Barr said the government looked set to undershoot its 26.4 billion sterling PSBR forecast, saying he expected a 26 billion figure for the year to April 1997.
